sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Fabric is an open-source command-line tool that organises AI prompts, called patterns, by real-world task. You pipe text, a web page or a YouTube video into a pattern like summarize or extract_wisdom, and get the result from the AI model of your choice.
sixtySeconds.problem: Good prompts get lost across chat apps and notes, and using AI inside everyday workflows means a lot of copy and paste. Fabric keeps a library of tested prompts and runs them from the terminal, so you can chain them with other command-line tools.
whoFor: Command-line users who want AI in their workflow
People who summarise articles, videos and papers
Developers who want a reusable prompt library
Anyone who wants to try many AI providers from one tool
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a large ready-made library of task prompts and one CLI that works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama and many other providers.
requirements: An API key for an AI provider, or a local model through Ollama

overview: Fabric's core idea is patterns: Markdown prompt files organised by task, like summarize, analyze_claims and extract_wisdom. You can run them through the fabric CLI or just read and copy them from the patterns folder.

Input can come from stdin, a URL (scraped to Markdown via Jina AI) or a YouTube video. Run fabric --setup once to choose your providers and enter keys. Supported providers include OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Ollama, Azure OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock, Vertex AI and LM Studio.

You can add your own patterns in ~/.config/fabric/patterns. Fabric also has a REST API server. It's written in Go and MIT licensed; older videos show the earlier Python version, so follow the current install steps.
